title: Double-label immunofluorescent staining of CD38 and oxytocin in the mouse hypothalamus
protocol: Anaesthetise the animal with pentobarbitone sodium at a dose of 50 mg/kg.
Incise the skin along the midline of the abdomen and expose the thorax.
Open the thoracic cavity to clearly visualise the heart and ascending aorta.
Insert a winged needle into the left ventricle and cut the right auricle as an exit for blood.
Perfuse the body with 20 ml of saline until the perfusate from the right atrium becomes translucent.
Change to fixative solution and perfuse the heart with a volume of 50 ml of fixative.
Incise and detach the dorsal head skin after perfusion.
Cut the boundary between the parietal and temporal bone.
Hold up the anterior brain and cut the optic nerve leaving the chiasma.
Carefully remove the brain tissue.
Cut the olfactory lobe and cerebellum.
Keep the anterior half of the brain for further procedures.
Cut perpendicular to the long axis into 5 mm thick tissue blocks.
Immerse tissue blocks with the optic chiasma in fixative for 3 h.
Wash brain tissue in PBS several times until picric acid fades to pale color.
Immerse tissue in PBS containing 20% sucrose and 0.05% azide at 4°C overnight for cryoprotection.
Freeze tissue in isopentane or acetone-dry ice mixture.
Pour OCT compound into an aluminum foil container.
Place a section of brain tissue on the bottom of the container.
Immerse the container with the tissue in cold isopentane.
Cut coronal sections of the brain tissue at a thickness of 20 μm on a cryostat.
Maintain the temperature of the knife and sample around -20°C.
Monitor the location of the section using a stereoscopic microscope.
Check for the hypothalamus by the presence of the optic chiasma.
Dry sections under cool air using a hair dryer for 15 min.
Wash sections in cold 1×PBS containing 0.3% TritonX-100 (PBST) at room temperature for 5 min.
Repeat washing step three times.
Remove 1×PBS and wipe the area surrounding the section.
Mark the boundaries of the area of the brain section on the slides using a DAKO pen.
Pipette 1% BSA and 5% normal donkey serum in 1×PBST containing 0.05% sodium azide onto the microscope slides.
Incubate for 45 min at room temperature.
Remove the BSA and normal donkey serum solution.
Pipette the primary antibody solution (usually 120-150 μl) onto the microscope slides.
Gently cover specimens with Hybribag film strips to minimize antiserum volume.
Transfer to a humid chamber.
Incubate overnight at 4°C.
Remove the strips carefully from the glass slides.
Wash the glass slides in 1xPBS for 5 minutes.
Repeat washing three times with 1xPBS.
Pipette Biotin-SP-conjugated AffiniPure Donkey anti-goat IgG \(1:400) as a secondary antibody solution onto the slides.
Incubate the slides with the secondary antibody solution for 60 minutes at room temperature.
Remove the secondary antibody solution from the glass slides.
Wash the glass slides in 1xPBS for 5 minutes.
Repeat washing three times with 1xPBS.
Pipette streptavidin-Alexa fluor 594 \(1:1000) onto the slides.
Incubate the slides with the streptavidin solution for 60 minutes at room temperature.
Remove the streptavidin solution from the glass slides.
Wash the glass slides in 1xPBS for 5 minutes.
Repeat washing three times with 1xPBS.
Pipette rabbit anti-mouse oxytocin \(1:500) onto the slides.
Incubate overnight at 4°C.
Remove the primary antibody solution from the glass slides.
Wash the glass slides in 1xPBS for 5 minutes.
Repeat washing three times with 1xPBS.
Pipette Alexa Fluor 488 conjugate anti-rabbit IgG as a secondary antibody solution onto the slides.
Incubate the slides with the secondary antibody solution for 60 minutes at room temperature.
Remove the secondary antibody solution from the glass slides.
Wash in 1×PBS for 5 minutes.
Repeat washing three times.
Pipette DAPI solution (1:1000) onto slides for nuclear staining.
Incubate for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Remove DAPI solution from the glass slides.
Wash in 1×PBS for 5 minutes.
Repeat washing three times.
Add anti-fade mounting medium to remove liquid.
Cover the samples with coverslips.
Include specimens from CD38 knockout (CD38-/-) mice as negative controls.
Omit the primary antiserum to test for specificity.
Omit the secondary antiserum to test for specificity.
Omit the avidin-biotin peroxidase complex to test for specificity.
Replace the primary antiserum with non-immune serum to test for specificity.
Replace the primary antiserum with pre-immune serum to test for specificity.
